title: The closest point on a line
description: Read the parameters, assemble the derivation, and explain why it works.
source_question_verbatim:
> Show that the point on the line y = mx which is closest to the point (a, b) is  $\left(\frac{a+mb}{m^2+1}, m\frac{a+mb}{m^2+1}\right)$ .

Source: `meckes_meckes_linear_algebra` ch_04, exercise 4.3.9.
display_problem: For fixed real m, a, and b, consider the line y = m*x and the point p = (a,b).
Show that the unique closest point in Euclidean distance is
The target answer is supplied. Your task is to build and justify its derivation.

solution.reason: Represent every point on the given line with one unknown t.
Choose t so the residual is perpendicular to the line.
The denominator is positive for every real m.
Scalar multiplication gives the supplied target coordinates.
For every real s, perpendicularity removes the cross term.
